build_platform: Windows x64; llvm-mingw UCRT; static C++ runtime
implemented: Bounded FE settings, animation attraction, curvature rods/hinges, ground and world collision data, zero-gravity engine compatibility
Authored quad import, native SubD topology and quad decompiler roundtrip; default offline Catmull-Clark subdivision for retail renderer compatibility
Point/Orient/Aim/Parent weighted constraint baking into ordinary animation
Scoped DMX dependency evaluation, layered logs, connections, expressions and pack/unpack operators

runtime.game: Installed CSGO legacy; offline -insecure local de_dust2
runtime.fixtures: Self-authored diagnostic meshes and animations only

tested: 20-point stock/NP proxies with one driven bone
map reload with three cloth models
cloth.observed: Visible cloth poses change and follow entity movement; zero-gravity and plane variants load and remain visible after map reload.
limits: One fitted bone gives rigid section motion, not per-proxy-vertex deformation.
Plane collision serializes and the sample animates; numerical proxy contact and absence of all rendered-vertex penetration are not established.
Stock/NP SIMD solve packet ordering differs; no frame-by-frame dynamic equivalence claim.
Engine-supplied world sphere/capsule colliders were not exercised.
cloth.fixed: CSGO treats descriptor gravity_scale 0 as 1; compiler writes descriptor 1 and per-node gravity 0.

constraints.discovery: Stock and initial NP procedural records 8/9/10/12 did not drive helper bones in installed runtime; source CalcProceduralBone has no cases for these types.
constraints.fix: Compile-time Point/Orient/Aim/Parent constraint baking into ordinary animation, removing ALWAYS_PROCEDURAL flag from these slaves.
constraints.observed: At approximately 1s and 3s samples, blue point helper follows target height, yellow orient changes direction, magenta aim points toward weighted target, cyan parent follows translated/rotated target. The stock metadata-only sample leaves these helpers ineffective.
constraints.limitations: Baking evaluates source frames before later QC processing; runtime blends and IK do not re-solve constraints.

subd.default: Two-pass offline Catmull-Clark baked into ordinary triangles
subd.observed: Rounded cube and curved grid both render as smooth surfaces in CSGO; model-only wireframe confirms subdivided triangles.
subd.native: Stock/NP native cube/grid all reproduce a null-buffer viewer crash; explicitly opt-in native export only for supported renderers.

reference_native_subd.retail_failure: Stock and NP native cube/grid AV at studiorender.dll+0x43cad after LockSubDBuffer returns null; installed materialsystem stub bytes 33 C0 C2 04 00.

limits: FE is limited to supported proxy maps and valid anchored skeletal meshes; a fitted bone does not reproduce every simulated vertex.
World sphere/capsule flags require runtime-supplied colliders, not verified here.
Native SubD requires a renderer with implemented SubD support; installed CSGO legacy/HLMV does not provide it.
Constraint baking occurs before later QC processing; runtime blends/IK and later QC edits do not re-solve constraints.
No new Linux execution or universal compiler/runtime parity is claimed.
remaining_outside_this_scope: AxisInterp import and material teeth flags
Additional DMX operator/curve types and broader cloth proxy schemas
